Cheers,

Sudeep 

PS: Side question, the output.csv was humongous because it wrote out samples from the posterior for each word -topic assignment in vocabulary and each document-topic assignment. Is there a way to condense the output?

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: LDA new document inference with STAN
parts:
I should clarify and say that anything declared in the "parameters" block is always saved. Anything declared and defined in the model block is discarded. Transformed parameters is somewhere in between. Anything declared at the top-level in transformed parameters is saved, but you can use local blocks within transformed parameters to avoid saving intermediate quantities. For example:

parameters {
 real x;
}
transformed parameters {
  real a;
 {
  real b;
  b <- 2;
  a <- x + b;
 }
}
model {
 real c;
 c <- x^2;
}

Here x and a will be saved but b and c will not.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] LDA new document inference with STAN
parts:
You want to just include those "new" documents in the original
model and fit everything at once. That gives you the full Bayes
solution. Having said that, you can't compute full Bayes for
LDA, so everything you do with this is going to be a hack (not
your fault, just the nature of LDA).

- Bob
